
##Geom package and variations

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
exists("geom_point")           # TRUE once ggplot2 is loaded
ls("package:ggplot2", pattern = "^geom_")   # lists all geoms available
```

#using mtcars dataset to apply geom_point, geom_smooth, geom_boxplot
```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point()
```

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()
```

##Using geom_smooth alone
```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```
#Using geom_boxplot to summarizes the distribution of a numeric variable, usually split by a categorical variable. It shows the median, spread, and outliers in one compact shape.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

##geom_histogram() splits the values into bins and draws a bar for each bin’s count
#how to use it using iris dataset
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Basic histogram
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram()

# Control the number of bins and style
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "steelblue", color = "white")

# Or set the bin width directly
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, fill = "steelblue", color = "white")

# Color by species (stacked by default)
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, color = "white")

# Overlapping instead of stacked
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity")

# One panel per species
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ Species)
```

#geom_density() draws a smooth curve estimating the shape of the distribution.
```{r}
# Basic density curve
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_density()

# Filled and styled
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_density(fill = "orange", alpha = 0.5, color = "darkred")

# One curve per species
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5)

# Smoother or wigglier curve
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_density(adjust = 2)     # larger = smoother
```

##Geom_line used for trends over time or any ordered sequence
#how to use it by using airquality: one month
```{r}
may <- subset(airquality, Month == 5)

ggplot(may, aes(x = Day, y = Temp)) +
  geom_line()
```
#one line per month
```{r}
# Month is numeric, so convert to factor
ggplot(airquality, aes(x = Day, y = Temp, color = factor(Month))) +
  geom_line()

# Or use separate panels
ggplot(airquality, aes(x = Day, y = Temp)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ Month)
```

#Full time series with a real date

```{r}
airquality$Date <- as.Date(paste(1973, airquality$Month, airquality$Day, sep = "-"))

ggplot(airquality, aes(x = Date, y = Temp)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue")
```

##geom_violin() draws a mirrored density curve for each group. The width of the shape at any height shows how many observations fall around that value. It combines the idea of a boxplot (comparing groups) with a density plot (showing the full shape)

#Applying it on ToothGrowth dataset built in R
```{r}
head(ToothGrowth)
tail(ToothGrowth)
str(ToothGrowth)
```

```{r}
ggplot(ToothGrowth, aes(x = factor(dose), y = len, fill = factor(dose))) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, fill = "white") +
  labs(title = "Tooth Length by Vitamin C Dose",
       x = "Dose (mg/day)",
       y = "Tooth Length") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
